summary.text: Mark Schaukowitch is the Democratic candidate for the Kansas House of Representatives, District 110, in the November 3, 2026 general election, facing Republican incumbent Ken Rahjes; he is a grant and technical writer in rural development.
In a Ballotpedia survey, he named property tax reduction, rural health care and housing among his priorities.

paragraphs.text: Mark Schaukowitch earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Kansas in 2009 and a graduate degree from Syracuse University in 2009, according to Ballotpedia.

In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he is a former adjunct professor of social advocacy at the University of South Carolina who returned to Plainville, Kansas, during COVID and began working on grants for local projects, including a nursing home replacement and rural water districts.

He said he helped start the Transparent Opportunities Speaker Series, worked with landowners and businesses to oppose a proposed Smithfield Foods hog farm near Plainville, and organized the county Democratic Party along with four other counties.
Schaukowitch advanced unopposed from the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary, receiving 496 votes.

He said he would seek a state incentive program for counties and municipalities that lower mill levies, a sovereign wealth permanent fund to eventually replace rural property taxes, state funding for elder care facilities, Medicaid expansion, and local land banks tied to healthcare worker housing.
He listed retired state Senator Janis Lee as an endorser.
